title: Platform systems & services 2026 Q1 runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap & retrospective (v2)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This consolidated reference provides Platform Engineering and SREs with runbooks, dashboard and alerting standards, operational how-tos, Q1 2026 roadmap highlights, and a short retrospective of major incidents and follow-ups. It is the canonical source for oncall run procedures and observability changes affecting systems & services.

Scope

- Core platform systems: API gateway (redwood-gw), model-router, inference-runtime, cache-proxy, telemetry-pipeline, identity-service
- Dashboards, alerts, and synthetic jobs used by oncall and platform product teams
- Runbooks for P0/P1/P2 incidents and post-incident actions
- How-tos for adding dashboards/alerts and performing routine maintenance and capacity ops
- Roadmap items that directly affect observability, reliability, and capacity planning

Ownership

- Platform Systems & Services (primary): Platform Engineering (pager: #platform-oncall)
- Observability & Dashboards: Monitoring team (secondary)
- Runbook maintenance: individual service owners (see runbook table)

Contents

1. Services, ownership, and key SLOs
2. Dashboard and alerting standards
3. Runbooks (P0/P1/P2) and common diagnostics
4. How-tos: add dashboard, add alert, perform capacity actions, cache maintenance
5. Q1 2026 Roadmap highlights and milestones
6. Retrospective: incidents, RCAs, and tracked action items
7. Appendix: example alert rules and contact list

1) Services, ownership, and key SLOs

- redwood-gw (edge/API gateway): Availability SLO 99.95%, request latency p95 < 120ms
- model-router: Availability SLO 99.9%, route decision latency p95 < 50ms
- inference-runtime: Availability SLO 99.5%, token latency p95 < 40ms for short requests
- telemetry-pipeline: Data completeness >= 99% for traces/metrics within 2 minutes

Primary owner: Platform Engineering (lead: Marcus Lee). Secondary owner: Infra Reliability. Pager channel: #platform-oncall.

2) Dashboard and alerting standards

Principles:
- Build dashboards for intent: "is the system serving traffic correctly?" then "is latency/cost within expected bounds?"
- Alerts must be actionable; avoid noisy or informational alerts that page the oncall rota
- Use three-tier policy: Pager (P0/P1), Slack-only (P2), Info (no immediate action)

Required dashboard panels per service:
- Availability & error budget with incident overlays
- Latency distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99) alongside request rate
- Resource utilization: GPU/CPU/memory, queue/backlog lengths
- Cost & throughput: tokens/sec, tokens/GPU
- Request breakdown by model, route, and customer tier

Example alert thresholds (tuned Q1 2026):
- redwood-gw: 5xx_rate > 1% for 5m -> P1 pager
- model-router: route_errors > 0.5% for 5m -> P1 pager; fallback_rate > 10% for 10m -> P0 pager
- inference-runtime: token_latency_p95 > 80ms for 10m -> P0 pager; GPU_throttling > 20% for 10m -> P1
- telemetry-pipeline: metric_ingest_failure_rate > 0.1% for 5m -> P1

3) Runbooks (P0/P1/P2) and diagnostics

P0 - System-wide outage or severe degradation (immediate steps):
1. Acknowledge the page and create incident channel (#incidents/<id>)
2. Triage scope: all customers / subset / region. Check global dashboards and fleet health panels
3. Apply mitigations in this order (least customer impact first):
   a. Reroute traffic to healthy region or model-variant using model-router fallbacks
   b. Increase reserved/dedicated capacity for critical tenants if available
   c. Enable targeted throttling on non-critical routes via gateway config
4. If mitigation not effective within 15 minutes, escalate to Eng Director and schedule a bridge
5. After stabilization: collect logs, traces, KV cache hit ratios, model load metrics; open postmortem draft within 48 hours

P1 - Service degradation (triage):
1. Acknowledge and record affected service/region/model in incident channel
2. For latency: check batch sizes, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization; optionally reduce batch window
3. For errors: inspect model-router logs, model load events, and recent config changes; rollback if needed
4. Document mitigation and create follow-up tasks for RCA

P2 - Minor issues / alerts:
1. Triage during business hours or queue for next oncall after-hours
2. Add to maintenance backlog if non-critical; monitor recurrence

Common diagnostics (examples):
- API gateway errors:
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/redwood-gw --since=10m | grep -i error | tail -n 200

- Token latency query (Prometheus):
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))

- Scale inference-runtime pool (infra CLI):
infractl capacity set --pool inference-prod --gpus 8

4) How-tos

How to add a new dashboard:
1. Draft Grafana JSON in monitoring repo: dashboards/platform/<service>-<short-name>.json
2. Include availability, latency, resource, and cost panels; add runbook links in panel descriptions
3. Submit PR to git@internal:redwood/monitoring-configs and request @platform-observability review
4. After 24h of no blocking feedback, schedule deploy to prod Grafana during low-traffic window

How to add or tune an alert rule:
1. Create rule in monitoring/alerts/<service>.yaml with labels: severity, owner_team, team_email
2. Include runbook link under annotations.href and a short actionable summary
3. Run linter: tools/monitoring-lint --path <file>
4. Submit PR and request Monitoring + Platform oncall review; deploy during low-traffic window and validate in staging with synthetic traffic

Controlled cache flush for inference-runtime:
1. Announce maintenance on #platform (15 minutes)
2. Execute: redis-cli -h cache-prod flushdb --async
3. Monitor KV cache hit ratio; rollback if error rate increases by >0.5% or latency spikes

5) Q1 2026 Roadmap highlights and milestones

- Observability: per-route latency heatmaps and per-tenant cost attribution (target 2026-03-15) - owner: Priya Shah (Monitoring)
- Reliability: fallback engine v2 with improved cold-start mitigation (target 2026-04-01) - owner: Marcus Lee (Platform)
- Capacity: dynamic burst pools alpha for Dedicated customers and GPU packing improvements (target 2026-05-01) - owner: Daniel Kim (Infra)
- Runbooks: consolidate service runbooks into central repo and add unit tests for alert rules (ongoing)

6) Retrospective: incidents (Jan-Feb 2026) and action items

Notable incidents:
- 2026-01-20: model-router misrouting caused elevated fallback rates and a 15m outage in eu-west. Root cause: config desync during canary rollout. Action: implement automated config verification and canary quorum check. Owner: Marcus Lee. Status: completed 2026-02-28.
- 2026-02-11: telemetry-pipeline lag (missing dashboards for ~12m). Root cause: Kafka broker GC pause. Action: increase replication for critical topics and add JVM flags to brokers. Owner: Priya Shah. ETA: 2026-03-10 (in progress)

Tracked action items:
- PLAT-324: config verification gate for model-router canaries (in progress)
- PLAT-338: synthetic traffic job to validate per-route latency heatmaps (todo)
- PLAT-346: runbook unit tests for alert rules (in review)

7) Appendix: example alert rule and contacts

Example Prometheus alert snippet:
- alert: InferenceRuntimeHighP95
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 0.08
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
    owner_team: platform
  annotations:
    summary: "Inference runtime p95 token latency > 80ms"
    description: "Check KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and recent deployments. See runbook: /runbooks/inference-runtime-p0"
